title: [webpack 2] `watch` & System.import compile with new chunk name
body:
I've search high and low; I don't think anyone has reported this yet.

I'm building an application using dynamic code splitting with `System.import`, as detailed [here](https://gist.github.com/sokra/27b24881210b56bbaff7#dynamic-expressions). I've got a build that spits out an entry point (`app.js`) and two chunks (`0.js` & `1.js`). However, when running with `--watch`, if I make a change in one of the dependencies of `0` or `1`, `webpack` rebuilds the chunk with a new name, ouputting a new `3.js` chunk instead of updating the already-built chunks.

Because the main `app.js` chunk hasn't changed, it continues to load the already-emitted chunk `0.js` or `1.js` chunk (depending on the page), so the changes don't actually show up in the loaded scripts.

Here's my `webpack.config.js`:

``` js
module.exports = {
    entry: {
        'app': './app.js'
    },
    devtool: 'sourcemap',
    debug: true,
    output: {
        path: './build/',
        filename: '[name].js',
        publicPath: './build/'
    },
    module: {
        loaders: [
            {
                test: /\.js$/,
                loader: 'babel'
            },
            {
                test: /\.hbs$/,
                loader: 'handlebars'
            }
        ]
    },
    resolve: {
        mainFields: ['jsnext:main', 'main']
    },
    plugins: []
};
```
